messages:
sam: Heads-up — apiserver 5xx spike in eu-west1 started ~10:12 UTC. etctd leader jumped 3x and controller-manager requeues spiked. GPU attach backlog increasing (attach lat >60s, many pods Pending).
maria: Looking at leader history — leader moved n1 -> n3 at 10:11, then n2 at 10:13. etcd commit latency up to ~300ms during hops. I'm seeing ICMP frag logs in VPC flow logs near the NAT.
jamie: Kernel logs on master-n3 show repeated fragmentation/clone warnings: `net: skb: can't clone skb` and lots of TCP retransmits. Did we change MTU or a NAT appliance recently? there was an egress NAT rollout earlier.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/egress-nat v2 promoted to eu-west1 at 09:58 UTC (:information_source: automated deploy record)
kevin: Confirmed: GPU provisioner control-plane traffic for attach goes out through egress-nat path. If PMTUD broke or MSS clamping changed, raft/keepalive packets could fragment and cause higher election timeouts.
sam: Mitigation options — quick: scale apiserver replicas in eu-west1 to 5, enable tcp_mtu_probing on masters, or rollback NAT rollout. Rollback is heavier during live traffic.
maria: Rollback might be risky. Recommend immediate steps: set `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on control-plane nodes, increase etcd election timeout to 10s (temporarily), and add short retry window on provisioner to smooth attach spikes.
jamie: I SSH'd master-n2, set `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and restarted kube-apiserver (graceful). After that leader stabilized and commit latency dropped ~300ms -> ~40ms. running canary for 15m.
ops-bot: alert-bot: apiserver 5xx rate down 85% in last 5m. :thumbsup:
kevin: Note on cost — GPU pending backlog caused cluster-autoscaler to launch extra worker nodes. We hit a brief burst of preemptible-like instances; added ticket INF-392 to cap burst and tweak backoff to avoid runaway cost.
sam: Next steps: 1) Confirm root cause — did egress-nat v2 change MSS/clamping or PMTUD handling? 2) Draft short postmortem and RCA once stable. 3) Follow-up: provisioner retries, canary limits, and autoscaler burst cap. Tagging eng-ml for any model-serving dependency.
maria: I'll add a runbook entry: "If etcd leader hops >2 in 5m in a region: enable mtu probing on masters, scale apiserver to 5, and notify oncall; consider NAT rollback if fragmentation persists." Opening PR for runbook now.
jamie: Leaving a small command snippet for reproduce/inspect: 
```
# check MTU and fragments
ip link show
sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing
sudo journalctl -u kube-apiserver -n 200 | grep -i frag
``` 
sam: Good work. I'll keep this thread updated if anything regresses. For now canary looks healthy, but keep eyes on leader hops and GPU attach tail latencies.
